questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman at 30 weeks' gestation has a routine complete blood count before a dental procedure. She feels well and her pregnancy has been uncomplicated. Her hematocrit is mildly lower than it was before pregnancy, and her physician tells her the finding is expected. Which of the following best explains this laboratory result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An absolute fall in red blood cell mass below baseline

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bone marrow suppression caused by rising estrogen levels

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased splenic destruction of maternal red blood cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Plasma volume expansion exceeding red blood cell mass expansion

choices.label: E
choices.text: Suppression of erythropoietin release by placental hormones

explanation.summary: Physiologic anemia of pregnancy is dilutional: plasma volume rises more than red cell mass.
explanation.whyCorrect: Blood volume rises 40%-50% in pregnancy, but red blood cell mass rises only about 20%. Because the plasma expands more than the red cells, hemodilution lowers the hematocrit, producing the physiologic anemia of pregnancy. Hemodilution actually stimulates erythropoietin, so red cell production increases even though the hematocrit stays below nonpregnant values.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Red blood cell mass rises by about 20%; it does not fall below baseline.
whyWrongByChoice.B: No marrow suppression is involved; red cell production actually increases.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pregnancy anemia is not hemolytic; the lecture attributes it to hemodilution.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Erythropoietin is stimulated, not suppressed, by the hemodilution of pregnancy.

questions.topicName: Pregnancy Effects on Other Organ Systems

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman at 22 weeks' gestation notes that her breasts have enlarged substantially, yet she has had no milk production. Histologic study of breast tissue at this stage would show fully developed alveoli capable of secretion. Which of the following hormones is chiefly responsible for preventing milk production at this point in pregnancy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Estradiol

choices.label: B
choices.text: Oxytocin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Progesterone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prolactin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Relaxin

explanation.summary: High progesterone levels hold milk production in abeyance during pregnancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: The breasts are developed enough to make milk by about 10-12 weeks, and prolactin drives alveolar differentiation into secretory epithelium by about 18 weeks. Milk production is nonetheless blocked throughout pregnancy by high levels of progesterone.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Estradiol contributes to early breast enlargement but is not the hormone blocking lactation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Oxytocin is not described as suppressing milk production during pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Prolactin promotes alveolar differentiation and polyamine production; it does not block milk production.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Relaxin acts on pelvic ligaments and vasculature, not on milk production.

questions.topicName: Pregnancy Effects on Other Organ Systems

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman at 12 weeks' gestation has thyroid function tests drawn at her first prenatal visit. She has no palpitations, heat intolerance, tremor, or weight loss. Her total thyroxine is elevated, while her free thyroxine is within the normal range. Which of the following best explains these results?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autoimmune thyroid gland hyperfunction with excess hormone release

choices.label: B
choices.text: Estrogen-stimulated hepatic production of thyroxine-binding globulin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Placental lactogen-driven rise in unbound circulating thyroxine

choices.label: D
choices.text: Progesterone-induced suppression of thyroxine-binding globulin synthesis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Relaxin-mediated reduction in hepatic clearance of thyroxine

explanation.summary: Estrogen raises thyroxine-binding globulin, increasing total thyroid hormone while free hormone stays stable.
explanation.whyCorrect: In pregnancy, estrogen stimulates the liver to make more thyroxine-binding globulin. More binding protein raises total thyroid hormone levels, but free (unbound, active) hormone remains relatively stable, so the patient is euthyroid.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A normal free thyroxine and absent symptoms argue against true hyperthyroidism.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Placental lactogen affects insulin resistance and lipolysis; free thyroxine is normal here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Binding globulin rises, not falls; a fall would lower total thyroxine.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Relaxin is not linked to thyroid hormone clearance in the lecture.

questions.topicName: Pregnancy Effects on Other Organ Systems

questions.stem: A physiology study tracks healthy women from conception onward and records serial cardiovascular and renal measurements. The investigators aim to identify the primary initial change that sets off the other hemodynamic adaptations of pregnancy, including changes in blood volume, cardiac function, and renal function. Which of the following changes is this initiating event?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An early fall in systemic vascular resistance

choices.label: B
choices.text: An early rise in myocardial contractile force

choices.label: C
choices.text: An early rise in renal sodium and water retention

choices.label: D
choices.text: An early rise in resting maternal heart rate

choices.label: E
choices.text: An early rise in total red blood cell mass

explanation.summary: The decrease in systemic vascular resistance is the primary initial driver of pregnancy's cardiovascular changes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Early in pregnancy, progesterone, estradiol, and relaxin cause systemic vasodilation, lowering SVR. The resulting 'underfilling' of the vascular tree prompts the kidneys to retain water and solutes, expanding plasma volume, and it is the stimulus for the subsequent changes in blood volume, cardiac function, and renal function.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Increased cardiac output follows increased blood volume and decreased afterload; it is not the trigger.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Renal sodium and water retention is a response to vascular underfilling caused by the fall in SVR.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Heart rate rises as part of the cardiac output response, downstream of the fall in SVR.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Red cell mass rises later, in response to hemodilution-stimulated erythropoietin.

questions.topicName: Pregnancy Effects on Other Organ Systems

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman at 35 weeks' gestation is lying flat on her back for a growth ultrasound. After several minutes she becomes lightheaded and nauseated, and her blood pressure falls to 86/50 mm Hg. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Give supplemental oxygen and keep her supine

choices.label: B
choices.text: Proceed with urgent cesarean delivery

choices.label: C
choices.text: Raise the head of the bed while supine

choices.label: D
choices.text: Start an intravenous vasopressor infusion

choices.label: E
choices.text: Turn her onto her left side

explanation.summary: Supine hypotensive syndrome is relieved by moving to the left lateral decubitus position.
explanation.whyCorrect: After about 20 weeks, the gravid uterus can compress the inferior vena cava and aorta when the patient lies supine, reducing venous return and cardiac output (supine hypotensive or aortocaval compression syndrome). Repositioning to the left lateral decubitus position restores blood flow and relieves symptoms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Remaining supine perpetuates compression of the vena cava and aorta.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This positional problem resolves with repositioning and does not require delivery.
whyWrongByChoice.C: She remains supine, so the uterus continues to compress the great vessels.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Vasopressors do not address the mechanical caval compression; repositioning does.

questions.topicName: Pregnancy Effects on Other Organ Systems

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman at 30 weeks' gestation has an arterial blood gas drawn during an evaluation for a minor injury; she has no respiratory complaints. The results show a pH of 7.44, a decreased PaCO2, and a mildly decreased serum bicarbonate. Her respiratory rate is 14/min, the same as before pregnancy. Which of the following best accounts for her low PaCO2?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A diaphragm-driven rise in breathing frequency

choices.label: B
choices.text: A fall in carbon dioxide output by maternal tissue

choices.label: C
choices.text: A primary renal loss of filtered bicarbonate

choices.label: D
choices.text: A progesterone-driven rise in tidal volume

choices.label: E
choices.text: An estrogen-driven rise in breathing frequency

explanation.summary: Progesterone raises tidal volume (about 40%) and minute ventilation without changing respiratory rate, lowering CO2.
explanation.whyCorrect: Minute volume increases in pregnancy even though the respiratory rate is unchanged, because tidal volume rises by about 40%, largely driven by progesterone. The extra ventilation lowers blood CO2 and alkalinizes the blood; the kidneys compensate by excreting bicarbonate, but pH still rises to about 7.44, a respiratory alkalosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The respiratory rate does not change in pregnancy, as her unchanged rate confirms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The low PaCO2 reflects increased ventilation, not reduced CO2 production.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The low bicarbonate is renal compensation for the respiratory alkalosis, not the primary event.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Respiratory rate stays the same; the increase in ventilation comes from tidal volume.

questions.topicName: Pregnancy Effects on Other Organ Systems

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman at 24 weeks' gestation has an abdominal ultrasound for an unrelated reason. Both kidneys measure about 1.5 cm longer than on imaging taken before pregnancy, and the renal collecting systems appear mildly dilated. She has no flank pain, fever, or urinary symptoms, and her urinalysis is normal. Which of the following best explains these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acute ascending pyelonephritis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bilateral renal artery stenosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Early autosomal polycystic kidney disease

choices.label: D
choices.text: Normal adaptation to higher renal flow

choices.label: E
choices.text: Obstructing stone in the left ureter

explanation.summary: In pregnancy, kidneys grow 1-2 cm and the collecting system dilates as renal blood flow and GFR rise.
explanation.whyCorrect: Renal blood flow rises 50%-85% and GFR rises 40%-60% in pregnancy. To adjust, the kidneys enlarge (from 10-13 cm by 1-2 cm in length) and the collecting system dilates. In an asymptomatic patient with a normal urinalysis these findings are physiologic.

whyWrongByChoice.A: She has no fever, flank pain, or urinary abnormalities to suggest infection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Renal blood flow increases in pregnancy; nothing suggests arterial narrowing.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Physiologic enlargement of pregnancy explains the findings without invoking cystic disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: She has no flank pain, and bilateral mild dilation with renal enlargement fits normal adaptation.

questions.topicName: Pregnancy Effects on Other Organ Systems

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman at 35 weeks' gestation presents with 3 days of nausea, vomiting, and malaise. She is jaundiced. Laboratory studies show a serum glucose of 48 mg/dL, elevated aminotransferases, and a prolonged prothrombin time. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Begin ursodeoxycholic acid with weekly fetal testing

choices.label: B
choices.text: Give intravenous fluids and antiemetics, then discharge

choices.label: C
choices.text: Perform appendectomy after surgical consultation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stabilize her and expedite delivery of the fetus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Start a proton pump inhibitor and reassess in 1 week

explanation.summary: Acute fatty liver of pregnancy is a third-trimester obstetric emergency treated by prompt delivery.
explanation.whyCorrect: GI symptoms in the third trimester accompanied by jaundice, hypoglycemia, elevated liver enzymes, and coagulopathy suggest acute fatty liver of pregnancy. Unlike hyperemesis gravidarum or appendicitis, AFLP can rapidly progress to maternal liver failure, fetal compromise, and death if prompt delivery is delayed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ursodeoxycholic acid is used for intrahepatic cholestasis, which causes itching without liver failure.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Supportive care alone treats uncomplicated vomiting; it delays the delivery AFLP requires.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Jaundice, hypoglycemia, and coagulopathy point to liver dysfunction, not appendicitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Acid suppression addresses reflux, not a life-threatening liver emergency.

questions.topicName: Pregnancy Effects on Other Organ Systems

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman at 31 weeks' gestation reports 2 weeks of intense itching that is worst on her palms and the soles of her feet. Examination shows excoriations but no primary skin lesions. Her fasting total bile acid level is elevated. Which of the following is the most appropriate medication to reduce her laboratory abnormality and her symptoms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Oral antihistamine

choices.label: B
choices.text: Oral folic acid

choices.label: C
choices.text: Proton pump inhibitor

choices.label: D
choices.text: Topical corticosteroid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ursodeoxycholic acid

explanation.summary: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy is treated with ursodeoxycholic acid plus close fetal monitoring.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pruritus without rash, especially of the palms and soles, with elevated fasting bile acids in the second or third trimester is intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy. Ursodeoxycholic acid reduces bile acid levels and symptoms; management also includes close fetal monitoring and typically planned delivery at 36-37 weeks.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An antihistamine does not lower the bile acids that drive the itching and fetal risk.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Folic acid supplementation does not address impaired hepatic bile flow.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Acid suppression treats reflux and has no role in cholestasis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: There is no rash to treat; the problem is impaired hepatic bile flow.

questions.topicName: Pregnancy Effects on Other Organ Systems

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman at 28 weeks' gestation presents with 2 days of swelling, pain, warmth, and redness of her left calf only. Compression ultrasound confirms a deep vein thrombosis. Which of the following physiologic changes of pregnancy most directly contributes to her hypercoagulable state?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Faster venous return from lower vascular resistance

choices.label: B
choices.text: Higher fibrinogen and factor VIII with less fibrinolysis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lower fibrinogen levels with heightened fibrinolysis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mild thrombocytosis from increased platelet production

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduced plasma volume that raises blood viscosity

explanation.summary: Pregnancy is prothrombotic: clotting factors rise and fibrinolysis falls, raising venous thromboembolism risk.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pregnancy increases fibrinogen and factors VII, VIII, and X and reduces fibrinolytic activity. Together with slowed venous return from uterine compression of the pelvic veins and IVC, this creates a hypercoagulable state that protects against postpartum hemorrhage but increases the risk of DVT and pulmonary embolism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Uterine compression slows, rather than speeds, venous return from the legs.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fibrinogen rises and fibrinolysis falls in pregnancy, the reverse of this option.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mild thrombocytopenia, not thrombocytosis, is common in pregnancy from platelet consumption.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Plasma volume increases in pregnancy; it does not fall.

questions.topicName: Pregnancy Effects on Other Organ Systems

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman at 26 weeks' gestation has a routine prenatal visit. Her pulse is 90/min, and her blood pressure is lower than it was before pregnancy. Cardiac auscultation reveals a soft systolic ejection murmur; she has no dyspnea, chest pain, or exercise limitation. Which of the following most likely accounts for the murmur?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreased circulating blood volume

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased stroke volume

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased systemic vascular resistance

choices.label: D
choices.text: Leaflet damage from prior endocarditis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Narrowing of the aortic valve orifice

explanation.summary: A physiologic systolic ejection murmur in pregnancy reflects increased stroke volume.
explanation.whyCorrect: Stroke volume rises in pregnancy in response to the increased blood volume and the marked fall in SVR (reduced afterload). The greater flow across the outflow tract produces a physiologic systolic ejection murmur, alongside the expected lower blood pressure and faster heart rate.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blood volume rises 40%-50% in pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: SVR falls in pregnancy, which is why her blood pressure is lower.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nothing in her history suggests valvular damage; the murmur is physiologic.
whyWrongByChoice.E: An asymptomatic patient with the expected vital-sign changes fits a flow murmur, not stenosis.

questions.topicName: Pregnancy Effects on Other Organ Systems

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman at 28 weeks' gestation undergoes metabolic testing as part of a research protocol. Compared with her prepregnancy values, her postprandial glucose is higher despite higher insulin levels, and her circulating free fatty acids are increased. Which of the following hormonal effects best explains both findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Estrogen reducing insulin resistance and fat breakdown

choices.label: B
choices.text: Placental lactogen raising insulin resistance and lipolysis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Progesterone raising insulin sensitivity and fat storage

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prolactin raising glycogen storage and fat storage

choices.label: E
choices.text: Relaxin reducing insulin release and lipolysis

explanation.summary: Placental lactogen raises insulin resistance and lipolysis, sparing glucose for the fetus and supplying fatty acids to the mother.
explanation.whyCorrect: Human placental lactogen increases maternal insulin resistance, so glucose remains higher after meals and is prioritized for the fetus, and it increases lipolysis, providing fatty acids as an alternative maternal energy source.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Insulin resistance increases in pregnancy, and fat breakdown is increased.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Insulin sensitivity falls in pregnancy, and fat breakdown, not storage, explains the fatty acids.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Prolactin prepares the breast for lactation; it does not explain insulin resistance.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Relaxin acts on vasculature and pelvic ligaments; lipolysis is increased, not reduced.

questions.topicName: Pregnancy Effects on Other Organ Systems

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman at 28 weeks' gestation is diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus after glucose tolerance testing. She had normal glucose levels before pregnancy. She asks why her blood sugar is now high. Which of the following best describes the underlying mechanism of her condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells triggered by placental antigens

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excess maternal cortisol suppressing glucose uptake by skeletal muscle

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fetal insulin crossing the placenta and down-regulating maternal receptors

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased renal glucose reabsorption raising the maternal glucose set point

choices.label: E
choices.text: Insulin resistance not matched by an adequate rise in insulin secretion

explanation.summary: GDM results from pregnancy-related insulin resistance that the maternal pancreas fails to compensate for with increased insulin secretion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Insulin resistance rises steadily through the second and third trimesters, so more insulin is needed to maintain euglycemia. A normal pancreas increases secretion to keep up; when the maternal insulin response is inadequate, maternal and then fetal hyperglycemia develop. GDM therefore reflects both insulin resistance and inadequate insulin secretion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Autoimmune beta-cell destruction describes type 1 (insulin-deficient) diabetes, not the insulin-resistance mechanism of GDM.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The lecture attributes pregnancy insulin resistance to placental hormones such as hPL, not to a cortisol excess.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The fetus makes its own insulin in response to maternal glucose; fetal insulin is not the cause of maternal hyperglycemia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: GDM is not caused by renal glucose handling; glucosuria is actually normal in pregnancy.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman at 26 weeks' gestation has rising postprandial glucose values and increased circulating free fatty acids compared with her first trimester. Which of the following hormones is primarily responsible for these changes, which help direct maternal glucose toward the fetus?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Corpus luteum progesterone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Human chorionic gonadotropin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Human placental lactogen

choices.label: D
choices.text: Maternal pituitary prolactin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ovarian relaxin

explanation.summary: Human placental lactogen (hPL) increases maternal insulin resistance and lipolysis, directing glucose to the fetus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pregnancy hormones rise steadily through the second and third trimesters and increase tissue insulin resistance. hPL is the hormone the lecture names as mediating this resistance and the accompanying increase in lipolysis, so postprandial glucose rises and glucose not taken up by maternal cells is used by the fetus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Corpus luteum progesterone is not the hormone that mediates late-pregnancy insulin resistance and lipolysis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: hCG is not the hormone that mediates the insulin resistance and lipolysis of late pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Prolactin is not identified as the mediator of pregnancy insulin resistance and lipolysis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Relaxin is not involved in pregnancy glucose metabolism in this way.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman comes for her first prenatal visit at 10 weeks' gestation. She asks whether anything in her history raises her chance of developing gestational diabetes mellitus. Which of the following features of her history is a risk factor for this condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Body mass index of 23 kg/m2 before pregnancy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Iron-deficiency anemia treated during adolescence

choices.label: C
choices.text: Polycystic ovarian syndrome diagnosed at age 19

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prior son weighing 7 lb 2 oz at birth

choices.label: E
choices.text: Seasonal allergic rhinitis treated with antihistamines

explanation.summary: A history of PCOS is a listed risk factor for GDM.
explanation.whyCorrect: Risk factors for GDM include age 25 or older, certain races/ethnicities, obesity (BMI >30), excessive gestational weight gain, prior glucose intolerance, history of PCOS, prior GDM, prior infant over 9 lb, multiple gestation, and family history of diabetes. Of the options, only her PCOS is on that list.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A BMI of 23 is not obese; obesity as a risk factor means BMI >30.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Iron-deficiency anemia is not a risk factor for GDM.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A prior infant counts as a risk factor only if large (>9 lb); 7 lb 2 oz is not.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Allergic rhinitis has no association with GDM.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman at 30 weeks' gestation has gestational diabetes mellitus that has been poorly controlled because she has not followed her dietary plan. She asks which problem is most likely to result. Which of the following is the most common complication of her condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fetal macrosomia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Neonatal hypocalcemia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Polyhydramnios

choices.label: D
choices.text: Preeclampsia

choices.label: E
choices.text: Umbilical cord prolapse

explanation.summary: Fetal macrosomia is the most common complication of GDM.
explanation.whyCorrect: High maternal glucose reaches the fetus, which is effectively overfed and grows larger than it should in utero. This fetal macrosomia (a large-for-gestational-age infant) is the most common complication of GDM and underlies the delivery complications such as shoulder dystocia.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Neonatal hypocalcemia is a recognized newborn risk but not the most common complication.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Polyhydramnios occurs in GDM but is less common than macrosomia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Preeclampsia is a major maternal complication of GDM, but not the most common complication.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cord prolapse is a downstream complication of polyhydramnios, not the most common GDM complication.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman at 32 weeks' gestation with gestational diabetes mellitus has fingerstick glucose values well above target. Ultrasound shows a markedly increased amniotic fluid volume and an accelerated fetal growth curve. Which of the following best explains the increase in amniotic fluid?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fetal hyperglycemia producing increased fetal urine output

choices.label: B
choices.text: Maternal glycosuria increasing the osmolality of the amniotic fluid

choices.label: C
choices.text: Placental overproduction of amniotic fluid stimulated by human placental lactogen

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reduced fetal swallowing from esophageal compression by the enlarged uterus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transudation of fluid across chorionic membranes from maternal hyperglycemia

explanation.summary: In GDM, fetal hyperglycemia causes fetal polyuria, and because amniotic fluid is largely fetal urine, polyhydramnios results.
explanation.whyCorrect: Maternal and fetal glucose levels are the same, so maternal hyperglycemia exposes the fetus to high glucose. The fetus develops increased urination (polyuria), and since amniotic fluid is basically fetal urine, this manifests as polyhydramnios. Fetal hyperinsulinemia also increases fat deposition, explaining the accelerated growth.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Maternal urine does not contribute to amniotic fluid; the source is fetal urine.
whyWrongByChoice.C: hPL mediates maternal insulin resistance and lipolysis; it does not produce amniotic fluid.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The lecture explains polyhydramnios in GDM by increased fetal urine production, not reduced swallowing.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Excess fluid in GDM comes from fetal urine, not transudation across membranes.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman with gestational diabetes mellitus delivers a 10-lb 4-oz boy vaginally. Delivery is prolonged because the anterior shoulder becomes impacted behind the pubic symphysis. After birth, the infant's right arm hangs limply at his side and he does not move the shoulder or elbow, but his right hand grasp is strong. Which of the following structures was most likely injured?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cervical spinal cord at the C3-C4 level

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lower trunk of the brachial plexus (C8-T1)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Right phrenic nerve in the neck

choices.label: D
choices.text: Right radial nerve at the spiral groove

choices.label: E
choices.text: Upper trunk of the brachial plexus (C5-C6)

explanation.summary: Shoulder dystocia in a macrosomic infant can stretch the upper brachial plexus, causing Erb palsy (C5-C6).
explanation.whyCorrect: Macrosomic infants are at risk for shoulder dystocia because the shoulders are the widest part of the body. Trauma to the shoulders and upper arms can cause brachial plexus injuries such as Erb palsy, a C5-C6 injury that weakens the shoulder and elbow while the hand is spared, as in this infant.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A cervical cord injury would produce bilateral and more widespread deficits, not a single limp arm.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A lower-trunk (C8-T1) injury would affect the hand; his grasp is strong.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Phrenic nerve injury affects the diaphragm and breathing, not arm movement.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Radial nerve injury at the spiral groove causes wrist drop, not loss of shoulder and elbow movement.

questions.stem: A term boy is born by cesarean delivery to a 34-year-old woman whose gestational diabetes mellitus was poorly controlled. Two hours after birth, he is jittery, and his serum glucose is 30 mg/dL. Which of the following best explains his low glucose level?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deficient hepatic glycogen stores from chronic placental insufficiency

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fetal hyperinsulinemia persisting after the umbilical cord is clamped

choices.label: C
choices.text: Impaired gluconeogenesis from liver immaturity related to prematurity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neonatal adrenal insufficiency from intrauterine glucocorticoid exposure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transfer of maternal insulin across the placenta just before delivery

explanation.summary: Fetuses of hyperglycemic mothers increase their own insulin production, which predisposes the newborn to hypoglycemia once the maternal glucose supply ends at birth.
explanation.whyCorrect: Maternal and fetal glucose levels are equal, so a fetus exposed to high glucose increases its own insulin production. After delivery, the maternal glucose supply is cut off, but the newborn's elevated insulin output persists, producing hypoglycemia, which is a listed postnatal risk for infants of mothers with GDM.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Placental insufficiency is not described in GDM; these fetuses are overfed and often macrosomic.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This infant is term, so prematurity-related liver immaturity does not apply.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Adrenal insufficiency is not a described complication of GDM.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The lecture describes the fetus producing its own excess insulin in response to glucose; maternal insulin transfer is not the mechanism.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman at 25 weeks' gestation drinks a 50-g glucose solution, and her blood glucose 1 hour later is 158 mg/dL. She has no symptoms. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Check a urine dipstick for glucose at each visit

choices.label: B
choices.text: Diagnose gestational diabetes and begin insulin therapy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obtain a hemoglobin A1c level to confirm the diagnosis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Perform a fasting 3-hour test with a 100-g load

choices.label: E
choices.text: Repeat the same 50-g screen in 4 weeks

explanation.summary: A 1-hour 50-g screen of 140 mg/dL or greater is followed by a fasting 3-hour 100-g glucose tolerance test.
explanation.whyCorrect: The 1-hour 50-g glucose screen is only a screening test. A result of 140 or greater fails the screen, and the patient proceeds to a fasting 3-hour test: a fasting glucose is drawn, she drinks 100 g of glucose, and glucose is drawn at 1, 2 and 3 hours and compared with predefined cutoffs.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Urine glucose is not useful because glucosuria is normal in pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A failed screen does not establish the diagnosis; confirmatory testing is needed, and lifestyle change, not insulin, is first-line.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hemoglobin A1c is not yet part of most official GDM diagnostic criteria.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A failed screen should be followed by confirmatory testing, not a repeat screen.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman at 27 weeks' gestation is diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus after a confirmatory glucose tolerance test. She has not yet received any treatment. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Begin twice-weekly nonstress tests now

choices.label: B
choices.text: Diet modification and regular exercise

choices.label: C
choices.text: Schedule induction of labor at 37 weeks

choices.label: D
choices.text: Start basal insulin at bedtime

choices.label: E
choices.text: Start metformin with meals

explanation.summary: First-line treatment of GDM is lifestyle modification: regular exercise and a structured diet.
explanation.whyCorrect: With confirmed GDM, the first-line treatment is regular exercise and a diet of 1800-2500 calories per day (40% carbohydrate, 40% fat, 20% protein). Most patients can manage GDM this way; medication is added only if glucose targets are not met.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antenatal fetal testing is done in the third trimester, not as the initial treatment at diagnosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Early induction is not part of the initial management described for GDM.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Insulin is used only if targets are not met despite diet and exercise.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Metformin is reserved for when lifestyle change fails and has less safety evidence than insulin.

questions.stem: Five women with gestational diabetes mellitus have followed diet and exercise for 2 weeks. Their typical fingerstick glucose values are listed below. Which patient's values indicate that pharmacologic therapy should now be added?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fasting 90 mg/dL; 2 hours after meals 115 mg/dL

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fasting 92 mg/dL; 2 hours after meals 118 mg/dL

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fasting 93 mg/dL; 1 hour after meals 148 mg/dL

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fasting 94 mg/dL; 1 hour after meals 136 mg/dL

choices.label: E
choices.text: Fasting 95 mg/dL; 2 hours after meals 120 mg/dL

explanation.summary: Medication is started when, despite lifestyle change, fasting glucose is >95 mg/dL, 2-hour postprandial >120 mg/dL, or 1-hour postprandial >140 mg/dL.
explanation.whyCorrect: The thresholds for adding medication are fasting fingerstick glucose >95 mg/dL, 2-hour postprandial >120 mg/dL, or 1-hour postprandial >140 mg/dL. Only the 1-hour postprandial value of 148 mg/dL exceeds a threshold.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Both values are within target.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fasting 92 and 2-hour 118 are both at or below the thresholds (>95 and >120).
whyWrongByChoice.D: A 1-hour value of 136 is below the >140 threshold, and fasting 94 is not above 95.
whyWrongByChoice.E: These values equal but do not exceed the thresholds; medication is started when fasting is >95 or 2-hour is >120.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman with gestational diabetes mellitus controlled by diet delivers a healthy infant. She asks whether she needs any further glucose evaluation now that the baby is born. Which of the following is the most appropriate plan?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Check glucose levels 24-72 hours after delivery

choices.label: B
choices.text: Continue the pregnancy diet plan for the next 6 months

choices.label: C
choices.text: Recheck the 50-g glucose screen at her 6-week visit only

choices.label: D
choices.text: Start metformin to prevent future type 2 diabetes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stop all glucose testing because the condition resolves

explanation.summary: Glucose is checked 24-72 hours postpartum to determine whether the patient actually has type 2 diabetes mistakenly diagnosed as GDM.
explanation.whyCorrect: GDM normally resolves shortly after delivery, and the patient can return to a normal diet. Glucose concentrations should still be checked 24-72 hours postpartum to distinguish hyperglycemia that was solely a product of pregnancy from type 2 diabetes misdiagnosed as GDM; persistent elevation requires diabetes treatment.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Once GDM resolves, the patient can return to a normal diet.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The 50-g screen is a pregnancy screening test; the lecture calls for glucose checks 24-72 hours postpartum.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Medication is not started prophylactically; treatment is needed only if glucose remains elevated.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Although GDM usually resolves, postpartum glucose testing is still needed to detect underlying type 2 diabetes.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman at 33 weeks' gestation has gestational diabetes mellitus with persistently elevated fasting glucose despite treatment. Her physician plans antenatal testing because poor control raises the risk of intrauterine fetal demise. Which of the following surveillance regimens is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Daily contraction stress tests until delivery

choices.label: B
choices.text: Monthly maternal hemoglobin A1c measurement only

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nonstress tests once or twice each week

choices.label: D
choices.text: Weekly amniocentesis for fetal lung maturity

choices.label: E
choices.text: Weekly maternal serum placental lactogen levels

explanation.summary: Third-trimester fetal surveillance in GDM includes nonstress tests one to two times weekly plus ultrasound.
explanation.whyCorrect: Poorly controlled GDM increases the risk of intrauterine fetal demise, so antenatal tests of fetal well-being are done in the third trimester. These include nonstress tests one to two times per week, which assess fetal heart rate patterns over time, and ultrasounds to assess well-being and amniotic fluid volume.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Daily contraction stress tests are not the described regimen; nonstress tests are used.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hemoglobin A1c does not assess the fetus and is not the monitoring tool described.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Serial amniocentesis is not part of the fetal surveillance described for GDM.
whyWrongByChoice.E: hPL levels are not used to monitor fetal well-being.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, comes for her first prenatal visit at 13 weeks' gestation. She has not seen a physician in several years. Her blood pressure is 148/94 mm Hg and, 4 hours later, 146/92 mm Hg. Urinalysis shows no protein. She has no headache, visual changes, or abdominal pain. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chronic hypertension

choices.label: B
choices.text: Eclampsia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gestational hypertension

choices.label: D
choices.text: HELLP syndrome

choices.label: E
choices.text: Preeclampsia

explanation.summary: Hypertension found before 20 weeks' gestation is classified as chronic hypertension.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chronic hypertension is high blood pressure that is preexisting or found before 20 weeks' gestation. Her readings exceed 140/90 mm Hg at 13 weeks, so the elevation is presumed to have preceded the pregnancy. Gestational hypertension and its related disorders develop only after 20 weeks.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Eclampsia is preeclampsia complicated by seizures; she has had no seizure.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gestational hypertension is new-onset hypertension that develops only after 20 weeks' gestation; she is at 13 weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HELLP syndrome requires hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelets; nothing suggests these.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Preeclampsia is diagnosed beyond 20 weeks and requires proteinuria or end-organ dysfunction; she has neither and is at 13 weeks.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old primigravida at 30 weeks' gestation has a blood pressure of 144/92 mm Hg, confirmed at 146/94 mm Hg 5 hours later. At 16 weeks her blood pressure was 112/70 mm Hg. She has no headache or visual changes. Urine protein is negative, and platelet count, creatinine, and liver enzymes are normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Close maternal and fetal monitoring without drug therapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Immediate induction of labor at 30 weeks' gestation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Magnesium sulfate infusion for seizure prophylaxis today

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral hydrochlorothiazide to reduce plasma volume now

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oral labetalol titrated to keep pressure below 140/90 mm Hg

explanation.summary: Gestational hypertension below the severe range is monitored closely; drugs are reserved for pressures above 160/110 mm Hg.
explanation.whyCorrect: She has gestational hypertension: new hypertension after 20 weeks with no proteinuria or end-organ dysfunction. Pharmacotherapy is generally reserved for severe hypertension (>160/110 mm Hg), so the correct approach is close monitoring of mother and fetus while watching for signs of preeclampsia, eclampsia, or HELLP syndrome.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Gestational hypertension without preeclampsia does not call for delivery at 30 weeks; it is monitored.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Magnesium sulfate is given for preeclampsia with severe features or eclampsia; she has neither proteinuria nor severe features.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Thiazide diuretics are among the drugs that are dangerous in pregnancy, and drug therapy is not yet indicated.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Labetalol is pregnancy-safe, but in gestational hypertension medication is reserved for severe-range pressures above 160/110 mm Hg.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman at 29 weeks' gestation with gestational hypertension has a blood pressure of 168/112 mm Hg, confirmed on repeat measurement 15 minutes later. Prompt treatment to lower her blood pressure is planned. Which of the following is the most appropriate medication?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chlorthalidone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hydrochlorothiazide

choices.label: C
choices.text: Labetalol

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lisinopril

choices.label: E
choices.text: Losartan

explanation.summary: Labetalol is one of the preferred antihypertensives in pregnancy; ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and thiazides are avoided.
explanation.whyCorrect: Severe hypertension (>=160/110 mm Hg) requires prompt treatment. The preferred agents in pregnancy are hydralazine, methyldopa, labetalol, and nifedipine ("Hypertensive Mothers Love Nifedipine"). ACE inhibitors/ARBs and thiazide diuretics are dangerous in pregnancy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chlorthalidone is a thiazide-type diuretic, a class to avoid in pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic, a class to avoid in pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lisinopril is an ACE inhibitor, a class that is dangerous in pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Losartan is an ARB, a class that is dangerous in pregnancy.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old primigravida at 33 weeks' gestation has a blood pressure of 150/96 mm Hg and, 6 hours later, 152/98 mm Hg. Her blood pressure was 114/72 mm Hg at 12 weeks. A 24-hour urine collection contains 480 mg of protein. Platelet count, creatinine, and liver enzymes are normal. She has no headache, visual symptoms, or seizures. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chronic hypertension

choices.label: B
choices.text: Eclampsia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gestational hypertension

choices.label: D
choices.text: HELLP syndrome

choices.label: E
choices.text: Preeclampsia

explanation.summary: New hypertension after 20 weeks on two readings at least 4 hours apart plus proteinuria >300 mg/24 h is preeclampsia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Preeclampsia is diagnosed beyond 20 weeks when blood pressure exceeds 140/90 mm Hg on two occasions at least 4 hours apart with proteinuria or end-organ dysfunction. More than 300 mg of protein in a 24-hour urine may indicate preeclampsia; she has 480 mg.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Her blood pressure was normal at 12 weeks, so the hypertension did not precede 20 weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Eclampsia requires new-onset seizures; she has had none.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gestational hypertension has no proteinuria or end-organ dysfunction; her 24-hour urine protein is 480 mg.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HELLP syndrome requires hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelets; her labs are normal.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman delivers at 34 weeks' gestation because of preeclampsia. Histologic study of the placental bed is performed. Compared with the maternal vessels supplying a normal placenta, which of the following best describes the vessels feeding her intervillous space?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Complete endothelial replacement by maternal fibroblasts

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excessively deep trophoblast invasion into the vessel wall

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased blood flow delivered into the intervillous space

choices.label: D
choices.text: Loss of smooth muscle producing wide low-resistance channels

choices.label: E
choices.text: Retained muscular media that remains vasoconstrictive

explanation.summary: Shallow cytotrophoblast invasion leaves spiral arteries unremodeled, with a responsive muscular wall that stays vasoconstrictive.
explanation.whyCorrect: Preeclampsia is associated with shallow cytotrophoblast invasion, which impairs spiral artery remodeling. The non-remodeled vessels keep an intact, responsive tunica media that remains vasoconstrictive, reducing blood flow to the intervillous space and causing placental oxidative stress and hypoxia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This is not the lesion; the vessels are intact and non-remodeled with a responsive muscular wall.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The defect is shallow, not excessive, cytotrophoblast invasion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Flow to the intervillous space is reduced, not increased, leading to placental hypoxia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Loss of the muscular wall is what normal remodeling achieves; in preeclampsia remodeling fails.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman at 35 weeks' gestation with preeclampsia with severe features is started on magnesium sulfate. One hour later her blood pressure is 166/112 mm Hg and, 15 minutes after that, 164/110 mm Hg. She has not had a seizure, and her reflexes are present. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add intravenous labetalol for blood pressure control

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add oral lisinopril for blood pressure control

choices.label: C
choices.text: Continue magnesium alone and recheck in 4 hours

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increase the magnesium dose until the pressure falls

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stop magnesium because it failed to lower pressure

explanation.summary: Magnesium sulfate prevents seizures but does not lower blood pressure; severe hypertension needs a separate antihypertensive.
explanation.whyCorrect: Acute severe hypertension (>=160/110 mm Hg) requires urgent treatment to reduce complications such as maternal stroke. Magnesium sulfate is given for seizure prophylaxis but is not an antihypertensive, so patients often need both magnesium and a pregnancy-safe blood pressure-lowering drug such as labetalol.

whyWrongByChoice.B: ACE inhibitors are dangerous in pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Severe-range hypertension requires urgent treatment to reduce the risk of maternal stroke.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Magnesium sulfate is not an antihypertensive; raising the dose will not treat the hypertension.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Magnesium is given for seizure prophylaxis, not blood pressure, and should continue.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman at 35 weeks' gestation is diagnosed with preeclampsia after blood pressures of 146/94 and 148/92 mm Hg taken 5 hours apart and a 24-hour urine protein of 400 mg. She has no headache, visual changes, or abdominal pain. Laboratory studies are normal, her pressure stays below 160/110 mm Hg, and fetal testing is reassuring. Which of the following is the most appropriate plan?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Close monitoring with delivery at 37 weeks' gestation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Delivery only after spontaneous onset of labor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Expectant management continued until 41 weeks' gestation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Immediate cesarean delivery at 35 weeks' gestation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Magnesium sulfate with induction within 24 hours

explanation.summary: Preeclampsia without severe features is monitored closely and delivered at 37 weeks.
explanation.whyCorrect: Delivery is the definitive treatment for preeclampsia, with timing based on gestational age and severe features. Without severe features, delivery is recommended at 37 weeks; before then, the patient and fetus are monitored closely.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Waiting for labor ignores the recommendation to deliver at 37 weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Delivery is recommended at 37 weeks, not continued pregnancy to 41 weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Immediate delivery is not indicated for stable preeclampsia without severe features before 37 weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Without severe features she does not need urgent magnesium and delivery at 35 weeks.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman at 36 weeks' gestation with a blood pressure of 162/108 mm Hg has a generalized tonic-clonic seizure in the labor triage unit. The seizure stops after 1 minute, her airway is protected, and she is placed on her side. Which of the following should be given to prevent further seizures?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hydralazine

choices.label: B
choices.text: Labetalol

choices.label: C
choices.text: Magnesium sulfate

choices.label: D
choices.text: Methyldopa

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nifedipine

explanation.summary: Magnesium sulfate is the drug of choice to prevent recurrent seizures in eclampsia.
explanation.whyCorrect: A seizure in a pregnant patient with hypertension after 20 weeks is eclampsia. Management is to administer magnesium sulfate to prevent additional seizures, stabilize the patient, and then deliver regardless of gestational age.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hydralazine is an antihypertensive, not seizure prophylaxis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Labetalol lowers blood pressure but does not prevent seizures.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Methyldopa is an antihypertensive, not seizure prophylaxis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nifedipine is an antihypertensive, not seizure prophylaxis.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman at 34 weeks' gestation comes to the emergency department with right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and vomiting. Her blood pressure is 154/100 mm Hg. Hemoglobin is 9.1 g/dL, platelet count is 68,000/mm3, AST is 310 U/L, and ALT is 280 U/L. A peripheral smear shows helmet-shaped and triangular red cell fragments. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Eclampsia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gestational hypertension

choices.label: C
choices.text: HELLP syndrome

choices.label: D
choices.text: Placental abruption

choices.label: E
choices.text: Preeclampsia without severe features

explanation.summary: Hemolysis with schistocytes, elevated transaminases, and thrombocytopenia define HELLP syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: HELLP syndrome is hemolysis (microangiopathic, with schistocytes), elevated liver enzymes, and low platelets. Symptoms, when present, include right upper quadrant pain and tenderness, nausea, vomiting, and headache. It is considered a severe form of preeclampsia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Eclampsia requires seizures; she has none.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gestational hypertension lacks end-organ dysfunction; she has hemolysis, liver injury, and low platelets.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Abruption presents with vaginal bleeding and abdominal pain, not schistocytes with elevated transaminases.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Her hemolysis, transaminase elevation, and thrombocytopenia are far beyond this; they define HELLP.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman at 30 weeks' gestation is found to have hemolysis with schistocytes, an AST of 290 U/L, and a platelet count of 72,000/mm3. Her blood pressure was 158/104 mm Hg and has been lowered with intravenous labetalol; magnesium sulfate is infusing. She has no active bleeding, and fetal heart rate tracing is reassuring. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Discharge home with twice-weekly laboratory checks

choices.label: B
choices.text: Expectant management until 34 weeks' gestation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Expectant management until 37 weeks' gestation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Proceed with prompt delivery at 30 weeks' gestation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Prophylactic platelet transfusion and continued pregnancy

explanation.summary: HELLP syndrome is treated by stabilizing the patient and delivering promptly regardless of gestational age.
explanation.whyCorrect: Delivery is the definitive treatment for any patient with HELLP syndrome. Once the mother is stabilized (antihypertensive, magnesium, blood products as indicated), delivery proceeds promptly regardless of gestational age.

whyWrongByChoice.A: HELLP is an obstetric urgency; outpatient management is unsafe.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Delaying to 34 weeks is a consideration only in select stable preeclampsia; HELLP calls for prompt delivery.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Waiting to 37 weeks applies to preeclampsia without severe features, not HELLP.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Platelets are given for active bleeding, and continuing the pregnancy is not appropriate in HELLP.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, comes for a prenatal visit at 10 weeks' gestation. Her previous pregnancy ended in an uncomplicated term vaginal delivery. Her history includes mild intermittent asthma, iron-deficiency anemia treated last year, an appendectomy at age 15, and type 1 diabetes mellitus since age 12. Which of the following in her history most increases her risk for preeclampsia?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Appendectomy at age 15

choices.label: B
choices.text: Iron-deficiency anemia treated last year

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mild intermittent asthma

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prior uncomplicated term vaginal delivery

choices.label: E
choices.text: Type 1 diabetes mellitus

explanation.summary: Preexisting medical conditions such as diabetes, hypertension, or kidney disease are risk factors for preeclampsia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Risk factors for preeclampsia include chronic hypertension, prior preeclampsia or pregnancy complications, family history, advanced maternal age, preexisting diabetes, hypertension, or kidney disease, first pregnancy, and multiple gestation. Her pregestational diabetes is the one listed risk factor.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A remote appendectomy is not a preeclampsia risk factor.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Treated iron deficiency is not a preeclampsia risk factor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Asthma is not among the risk factors for preeclampsia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: First pregnancy is the risk factor; a prior uncomplicated pregnancy does not add risk.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman at 35 weeks' gestation with HELLP syndrome begins oozing blood from her intravenous sites and gums. Prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time are prolonged, fibrinogen is low, D-dimer is markedly elevated, and platelet count is 32,000/mm3. Which of the following best explains her bleeding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autoantibodies directed against factor VIII

choices.label: B
choices.text: Consumption of clotting factors by systemic coagulation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inherited deficiency of von Willebrand factor

choices.label: D
choices.text: Isolated platelet destruction with normal clotting factors

choices.label: E
choices.text: Magnesium sulfate blockade of platelet adhesion

explanation.summary: HELLP can cause DIC, in which widespread clotting consumes coagulation factors and causes profuse bleeding.
explanation.whyCorrect: Disseminated intravascular coagulation is a serious complication of HELLP syndrome. Systemic activation of the coagulation cascade deposits clots throughout the body, causing ischemic organ damage, and consumes coagulation factors, causing profuse bleeding. Prolonged PT/PTT, low fibrinogen, and high D-dimer fit this picture.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An acquired factor VIII inhibitor would not explain low fibrinogen, high D-dimer, and thrombocytopenia in HELLP.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An inherited defect would not newly cause low fibrinogen and prolonged PT with HELLP.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Her prolonged PT/PTT and low fibrinogen show clotting factors are also depleted.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This is not the mechanism; the laboratory picture shows factor consumption.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman at 10 weeks' gestation by dates has vaginal bleeding. Transvaginal ultrasound shows a uterus filled with innumerable small cystic spaces and no fetal parts. Cytogenetic analysis of the evacuated tissue shows a 46,XX karyotype in which every chromosome is paternal in origin. Which of the following best explains how this lesion arose?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A diploid ovum from meiotic failure was fertilized by one sperm

choices.label: B
choices.text: A normal ovum was fertilized by one sperm, then lost a set

choices.label: C
choices.text: A normal ovum was fertilized by two sperm at once

choices.label: D
choices.text: An empty ovum was fertilized by one sperm that then duplicated

choices.label: E
choices.text: An ovum duplicated its own genome without sperm contribution

explanation.summary: A complete mole lacks the maternal genome: an empty ovum is fertilized by one sperm that undergoes mitosis (or by two sperm), usually giving 46,XX.
explanation.whyCorrect: A complete mole forms when the maternal genome is absent. Most often a single sperm fertilizes an empty ovum and duplicates by mitosis, producing a diploid, entirely paternal 46,XX conceptus with no fetal parts; less often two sperm fertilize the empty ovum.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A diploid ovum plus a sperm would give a triploid conceptus containing maternal DNA, not a purely paternal diploid mole.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This is not a mechanism the lecture describes, and it would not produce a genome that is entirely paternal.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Two sperm fertilizing a normal ovum produces a triploid partial mole (69 chromosomes) with maternal DNA and fetal parts.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Complete moles have no maternal genome; this scenario would be entirely maternal, the opposite of what cytogenetics shows.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman undergoes uterine evacuation after an ultrasound at 12 weeks shows a fetus with an abnormal, focally cystic placenta. Pathology shows two populations of villi, small fibrotic villi and scattered edematous hydropic villi, with focal trophoblastic hyperplasia and nucleated fetal erythrocytes in villous vessels. Which of the following additional findings is most expected in this tissue?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diffuse, circumferential hyperplasia of all trophoblast

choices.label: B
choices.text: Diploid karyotype composed only of paternal chromosomes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nests of mononucleated cells splitting myometrial fibers

choices.label: D
choices.text: p57 staining in cytotrophoblast and stromal cell nuclei

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sheets of cytotrophoblast with no villi in the specimen

explanation.summary: Partial moles are p57-positive in villous cytotrophoblast and stromal nuclei because they contain maternal genetic material.
explanation.whyCorrect: Two villous populations, limited trophoblastic hyperplasia, and fetal erythrocytes describe a partial mole. Because a partial mole arises from a normal ovum fertilized by two sperm, it carries maternal DNA, which immunohistochemistry reveals as p57 positivity in villous cytotrophoblast and stromal nuclei.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Diffuse, marked trophoblastic hyperplasia with uniformly edematous villi is the complete-mole pattern; partial moles have fewer hyperplastic trophoblasts.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A diploid, all-paternal genome describes a complete mole; partial moles are triploid and include a maternal set.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mononucleated intermediate trophoblast splitting the myometrium is the picture of placental site trophoblastic tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trophoblast sheets without villi define choriocarcinoma, not a partial mole, which has villi.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman at 11 weeks' gestation has heavy sweating, palpitations, and a 4-kg weight loss. Her pulse is 124/min. Ultrasound shows a heterogeneous intrauterine mass with multiple cystic spaces and no fetus. Serum hCG is 240,000 mIU/mL, TSH is suppressed, and free T4 is elevated. Which of the following best explains her thyroid findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autoantibodies that stimulate the thyrotropin receptor

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct secretion of free T4 by the proliferating trophoblast

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estrogen-driven increase in thyroxine-binding globulin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Human placental lactogen stimulating thyroid follicular cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Weak activation of TSH receptors by structurally similar hCG

explanation.summary: Markedly elevated hCG from a molar pregnancy weakly activates TSH receptors, causing clinical hyperthyroidism.
explanation.whyCorrect: hCG is structurally similar to TSH. At the marked elevations seen with molar pregnancy, hCG weakly stimulates TSH receptors, producing hyperthyroidism with perspiration, weight loss, and tachycardia, while pituitary TSH is suppressed by feedback.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Receptor-stimulating autoantibodies describe an autoimmune thyroid process; the lecture attributes molar hyperthyroidism to hCG itself.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Trophoblast produces hCG, not thyroid hormone; the free T4 comes from the stimulated thyroid gland.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A rise in binding globulin changes total, not free, hormone and would not cause suppressed TSH with thyrotoxic symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.D: hPL is the marker associated with placental site trophoblastic tumor; it is not the hormone that cross-reacts with TSH receptors.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman had a spontaneous abortion 5 months ago. She now has irregular vaginal bleeding and a markedly elevated serum hCG. A hemorrhagic, necrotic mass is found invading the uterine wall and is biopsied. Which of the following histologic findings is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chorionic villi embedded within the invaded myometrium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enlarged hydropic villi with circumferential trophoblast

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mixed small fibrotic and hydropic villi with fetal cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mononucleated cells with uniform nuclei, splitting muscle

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sheets of cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast, no villi

explanation.summary: Choriocarcinoma consists of sheets of cytotrophoblasts and syncytiotrophoblasts with hemorrhage and necrosis, and no chorionic villi.
explanation.whyCorrect: A hemorrhagic, necrotic uterine mass with very high hCG after a nonmolar pregnancy suggests choriocarcinoma. Histologically it is composed of sheets of the two placental cell types, pale cytotrophoblasts and dark multinucleate syncytiotrophoblasts, with mitoses and hemorrhage; unlike moles, villi are not evident.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Villi within invaded myometrium define an invasive mole; the absence of villi separates choriocarcinoma from it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hydropic villi with circumferential trophoblastic hyperplasia describe a complete mole, which contains villi.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Two populations of villi with fetal cells describe a partial mole.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Uniform mononucleated intermediate trophoblast splitting smooth muscle is placental site trophoblastic tumor, which has low hCG.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman is diagnosed with a complete hydatidiform mole at 9 weeks' gestation. She is hemodynamically stable, her hCG is 60,000 mIU/mL, and she hopes to have children in the future. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Expectant management with a repeat ultrasound in 4 weeks

choices.label: B
choices.text: Methotrexate as the sole treatment, without evacuation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Multi-agent chemotherapy with etoposide and dactinomycin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Suction curettage followed by serial serum hCG levels

choices.label: E
choices.text: Total hysterectomy with preservation of the ovaries

explanation.summary: Molar pregnancies are removed by suction curettage, followed by serial hCG monitoring until normalization.
explanation.whyCorrect: A molar pregnancy should be treated promptly, typically by suction curettage. Afterward, serial hCG measurements continue until normalization and through a surveillance period, during which pregnancy is avoided so rising hCG can be interpreted.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Treatment should begin once a mole is detected to prevent further symptoms; observation is inappropriate.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Methotrexate is added prophylactically for high-risk moles, not used alone in place of evacuation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Multi-agent regimens are used for choriocarcinoma, not first-line for an uncomplicated mole.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hysterectomy is an option only for a patient who does not plan to become pregnant again; this patient wants future children.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman delivered a healthy term infant 7 months ago. She now has irregular vaginal bleeding and a markedly elevated serum hCG, and evaluation shows a hemorrhagic uterine tumor composed of trophoblast without villi. Staging is planned. Which of the following sites is most likely to harbor metastatic disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Brain

choices.label: C
choices.text: Kidney

choices.label: D
choices.text: Liver

choices.label: E
choices.text: Lungs

explanation.summary: Choriocarcinoma metastasizes most commonly to the lungs (about 50%), then the vagina (30%-40%).
explanation.whyCorrect: This is choriocarcinoma after a normal gestation. It metastasizes early and often; the lungs are the most common site (about 50%), where lesions cause hemoptysis and appear as cannonball masses on chest x-ray.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bone is among the less common metastatic sites.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The brain is a less common site than the lungs and vagina.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The kidney is among the less common metastatic sites.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The liver is listed among the less common metastatic sites of choriocarcinoma.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman has had amenorrhea for 14 months since an uncomplicated term delivery. Serum hCG is only mildly elevated, and serum human placental lactogen is increased. Imaging shows a well-circumscribed 5-cm uterine mass with no evidence of spread beyond the uterus. Biopsy shows nests of mononucleated cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm infiltrating between smooth muscle fibers. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hysterectomy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Multi-agent etoposide and dactinomycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Observation with serial hCG levels

choices.label: D
choices.text: Single-agent methotrexate chemotherapy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Suction curettage

explanation.summary: Placental site trophoblastic tumor is treated primarily surgically, most commonly by hysterectomy for localized disease; chemotherapy is less effective.
explanation.whyCorrect: Elevated hPL with a comparatively low hCG, a circumscribed mass, and intermediate trophoblast splitting the myometrium after a normal pregnancy indicate a placental site trophoblastic tumor. Unlike other gestational trophoblastic neoplasms, it responds less well to chemotherapy, so hysterectomy is the main treatment for localized disease.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Multi-agent chemotherapy is used for choriocarcinoma, which is extremely chemo-sensitive, unlike PSTT.
whyWrongByChoice.C: hCG is relatively low in PSTT and a subset behave aggressively; localized disease should be removed surgically.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Single-agent methotrexate suits early choriocarcinoma or high-risk moles; chemotherapy is less effective for PSTT.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Suction curettage evacuates molar tissue but does not treat a tumor that infiltrates the myometrium.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman underwent suction curettage for a complete mole 10 weeks ago. Her serum hCG initially fell, then plateaued and began to rise, and she has recurrent vaginal bleeding. A hysterectomy specimen shows hydropic chorionic villi with proliferating trophoblast penetrating deep into the myometrium and its vessels. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Choriocarcinoma

choices.label: B
choices.text: Incomplete abortion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Invasive mole

choices.label: D
choices.text: Partial hydatidiform mole

choices.label: E
choices.text: Placental site trophoblastic tumor

explanation.summary: An invasive mole is a persistent molar gestation that invades the myometrium and its blood supply; villi remain evident.
explanation.whyCorrect: About 15% of complete moles progress to an invasive mole, which presents with vaginal bleeding and persistently elevated hCG after evacuation. Microscopically villi are still present within the invaded myometrium, which separates it from choriocarcinoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Choriocarcinoma also follows complete moles, but villi are not evident on its pathology.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An incomplete abortion does not produce rising hCG with villi invading the myometrium and vessels.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A partial mole contains fetal tissue and a mix of normal and hydropic villi; it is not defined by myometrial invasion after evacuation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: PSTT consists of intermediate trophoblast without hydropic villi and has relatively low hCG.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman at 11 weeks' gestation has vaginal bleeding and persistent nausea and vomiting. Her uterus is palpable well above the size expected for her dates, and serum hCG is 190,000 mIU/mL. Which of the following transvaginal ultrasound findings is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Empty uterus with a complex adnexal mass and free fluid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fetus with focal cystic change in an otherwise normal placenta

choices.label: C
choices.text: Live fetus with a normal-appearing, homogeneous placenta

choices.label: D
choices.text: Snowstorm pattern of cystic spaces with no fetal parts

choices.label: E
choices.text: Well-circumscribed solid mass infiltrating the myometrium

explanation.summary: A complete mole shows a snowstorm or bunch-of-grapes pattern with no fetal parts on ultrasound, reflecting cystic dilation of chorionic villi.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bleeding, hyperemesis, a uterus larger than dates, and hCG above 100,000 mIU/mL point to a complete mole. It is readily detected on ultrasound because no fetal parts are present, and the cystically dilated villi produce the characteristic snowstorm appearance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An empty uterus with an adnexal mass suggests ectopic pregnancy, not a molar gestation that enlarges the uterus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fetal parts with focal cystic placental change fit a partial mole, which usually has hCG closer to the normal pregnancy range.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A normal intrauterine pregnancy would not explain excess uterine size with hCG this high.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A solid, circumscribed myometrial mass is more typical of placental site trophoblastic tumor, which has low hCG.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman who has never been pregnant presents with pelvic pain and is found to have an ovarian mass and a markedly elevated serum hCG. Resection shows sheets of cytotrophoblast and multinucleate syncytiotrophoblast with extensive hemorrhage and no villi. Which of the following findings would best establish that this tumor is not of gestational origin?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absence of chorionic villi anywhere in the tumor

choices.label: B
choices.text: Absence of paternally derived DNA in tumor cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Extensive hemorrhage and necrosis in the gross specimen

choices.label: D
choices.text: Presence of both cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serum hCG level above 100,000 mIU/mL

explanation.summary: Nongestational choriocarcinomas are morphologically identical to gestational ones but lack paternally derived DNA, which all gestational choriocarcinomas contain.
explanation.whyCorrect: A small percentage of choriocarcinomas arise in the ovary or testis as germ cell tumors. They look the same microscopically as gestational choriocarcinoma, so morphology cannot separate them; the distinguishing feature is the absence of paternally derived DNA, which is present in every gestational choriocarcinoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lack of villi is shared by all choriocarcinomas and does not indicate origin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hemorrhage and necrosis are gross features of choriocarcinoma generally, not markers of nongestational origin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Both gestational and nongestational choriocarcinomas are made of the two trophoblast types; they are morphologically identical.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Markedly elevated hCG occurs with choriocarcinoma of either origin.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman is seen 1 week after suction curettage for a complete hydatidiform mole. She is recovering well and asks when she can try to conceive again. Which of the following is the most appropriate counseling?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Avoid pregnancy during hCG surveillance so a rise can be interpreted

choices.label: B
choices.text: Avoid pregnancy permanently, since future gestations are contraindicated

choices.label: C
choices.text: Conceive after one normal hCG level, since surveillance then stops

choices.label: D
choices.text: Conceive once bleeding stops, since hCG testing is only done if symptoms recur

choices.label: E
choices.text: Try to conceive right away, since hCG is not followed after evacuation

explanation.summary: After molar evacuation, serial hCG is followed until normalization and through a surveillance period, during which pregnancy is avoided so hCG results remain accurate.
explanation.whyCorrect: Serial hCG monitoring is required after evacuation until normalization and for an additional surveillance period. A new pregnancy would raise hCG and mask persistent or malignant trophoblastic disease, so the patient should avoid pregnancy during this time; afterward, successful pregnancy is possible.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Pregnancy is not permanently contraindicated; many patients go on to have healthy pregnancies after surveillance.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Monitoring continues beyond normalization for an additional surveillance period, not just until one normal level.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Surveillance is routine and scheduled, not symptom-triggered, because transformation can be silent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: hCG must be followed after evacuation; an immediate pregnancy would confound that surveillance.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman develops hemoptysis and rising hCG 3 months after evacuation of a complete mole. Chest x-ray shows multiple circumscribed pulmonary masses, and imaging also shows liver lesions. Biopsy shows trophoblast without villi. She wishes to preserve her fertility. Which of the following is the most appropriate approach?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hysterectomy alone, because chemotherapy is largely ineffective

choices.label: B
choices.text: Multi-agent chemotherapy with curative intent

choices.label: C
choices.text: Palliative care, because widely metastatic disease is incurable

choices.label: D
choices.text: Radiation to the lung masses, then serial hCG levels

choices.label: E
choices.text: Repeat suction curettage, then observation with hCG

explanation.summary: Choriocarcinoma is extremely chemo-sensitive; even widely metastatic disease can be cured with chemotherapy, often preserving fertility.
explanation.whyCorrect: This is metastatic choriocarcinoma after a complete mole. Early disease is treated with single-agent methotrexate, and more extensive disease with multi-agent regimens that may include etoposide and dactinomycin. Because the tumor is extremely chemo-sensitive, cure is possible even with wide metastases, and fertility can be preserved in many patients.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Poor chemo-responsiveness describes placental site trophoblastic tumor, not choriocarcinoma; hysterectomy alone also sacrifices fertility.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Metastatic choriocarcinoma is often curable, so a palliative-only approach is inappropriate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Radiation is not the treatment the lecture describes; systemic chemotherapy addresses widespread disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Curettage treats molar pregnancy; it does not address metastatic choriocarcinoma.
